title: Version-Control Your Automation
objective: Use a safe Git workflow to preserve and review infrastructure changes.

sourceAlignment.title: Getting started with Ansible 03 - Setting up the Git Repository
sourceAlignment.creator: LearnLinuxTV
sourceAlignment.note: English captions informed topic alignment and timestamps. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: Infrastructure code needs the same history and review discipline as application code. A repository records inventories, playbooks, roles, documentation, and dependency declarations as a sequence of explainable changes.

The basic loop is clone, edit, inspect the diff, stage intentional files, commit with a useful message, and push when an external remote is appropriate. Never stage secret keys, plaintext vault passwords, or generated credentials.
Small commits make troubleshooting easier because each change has one purpose. Before every commit, use git status and git diff --staged to verify exactly what the repository will preserve.
explanation.rule: Commit reviewed automation and documentation; keep credentials and generated secrets out of Git.

feedback.correct: Correct—this matches the demonstrated workflow and keeps the automation explicit.

checks.question: Which practice best supports this lesson’s objective: “Use a safe Git workflow to preserve and review infrastructure changes.”?
options: Preview scope, use state-aware modules, and verify the observed result.
Hide failures and assume the target state was reached.
Store credentials beside the playbook in plaintext.
Replace every module with an unreviewed shell command.

feedback.correct: Correct—safe automation combines explicit scope, desired state, and verification.
feedback.incorrect: The reliable workflow makes scope, state, and verification visible.

lab.title: Practice locally without pushing
lab.setup: Start the disposable lab with npm run lab:up, then work from /workspace in the Terminal tab.
steps: Create or edit a harmless README note.
Use git diff, but do not add credentials or push from the lab.
lab.success: Git shows only the intentional documentation change.
